title: Per-customer priority buckets with time-decayed overdraft credits PRD
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Problem: customers on higher-tier plans need predictable burst behavior but also want flexible short-term headroom when traffic spikes. Existing global soft-overage model is coarse (global credits, manual reconciliation) and leads to unexpected throttles for some tenants and stale billing disputes.

Proposal: introduce per-customer priority buckets plus a time-decayed overdraft credit mechanism. Each customer will have multiple logical priority buckets (e.g., high-priority routed traffic, standard generation, embeddings) with configurable baseline quotas. When a bucket exhausts quota, requests should attempt to consume per-customer overdraft credits that decay over a configurable time window (e.g., 24h half-life) rather than immediately triggering hard throttles or generating invoices for instant overage. The system aims to: reduce customer-facing failures during short spikes, make billing clearer by attributing overdraft usage to specific buckets, and enable automated reconciliation/crediting for transient incidents.
requirements: Support configurable priority buckets per customer: names, baseline quota (units/day), and priority order.
Implement a per-customer overdraft credit ledger: balance, issuance rules, decay profile (half-life or linear), and max overdraft cap.
Routing logic: when baseline quota for a bucket is exhausted, attempt to serve using overdraft credits; if overdraft exhausted or disabled, fallback to per-plan throttling behavior.
Billing attribution: overdraft usage must be recorded per-customer, per-bucket and available in the billing exports (CSV/BigQuery) and Console usage views.
Admin UX: in Console, show priority bucket configuration, current balances, recent overdraft events, and an override to replenish or revoke overdraft credits for support ops.
Audit trails: every overdraft debit/credit must have an immutable audit entry with timestamp, request-id, and reason code.
API/SDK behavior: new 429 subtype or response payload field indicating 'throttled:overdraft' vs 'throttled:quota' for downstream handling.
Simulation mode: ability to simulate overdraft consumption for a customer without affecting billing to test policies pre-rollout.
Migration: customers currently using global soft-overage should be automatically provisioned a default overdraft profile; provide a migration script and opt-out mechanism.
Observability: dashboards for overdraft utilization by percentile, per-plan leakage rate, and cost-impact estimates for the last 90 days.
Security: overdraft admin actions require RBAC privilege and are logged to audit loging service (KMS/HSM not required for this feature itself).
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: For a test tenant with baseline 100k tokens/day on 'standard' bucket and overdraft cap 50k tokens with 24h decay, a 30k token spike is served from overdraft and the balance reduces accordingly; Console shows correct debit with timestamp.
AC-2: If overdraft cap reached, further requests to that bucket return 429 with response metadata 'reason=throttled:overdraft' within 500ms of enforcement; no requests are silently dropped.
AC-3: Billing export contains per-customer, per-bucket overdraft usage column and matches ledger totals for a 7-day integration test (tolerance < 0.1%).
AC-4: Simulation mode toggled for customer X (via Console and API) produces identical policy decisions but does not alter ledger balances or billing exports; logs annotate 'simulation=true'.
AC-5: Admin override flow in Console for increasing overdraft cap creates an audit entry, requires RBAC permission 'billing.admin', and the override becomes effective within 30s.
AC-6: Migration script provisions default overdraft profile for 95% of existing soft-overage customers without downtime; migration runbook documented and reversible.

AC-7: Observability dashboard surfaces at least these metrics: overdraft usage rate, percent of requests served from overdraft, number of customers with >50% overdraft utilization; dashboards load under 3s for 90-day window.

AC-8: End-to-end integration test simulating multi-bucket spike (high-priority then standard) validates priority ordering: high-priority consumes baseline first, then overdraft; standard is unaffected until high-priority returns to baseline.

AC-9: Product and finance sign-off: finance confirms that overdraft ledger entries can be reconciled to invoices and agrees on the reporting columns; product confirms UX acceptance in a recorded demo.
AC-10: Security review sign-off if customer opts-in to on-prem/private (if security_review_required flag true) — note: for hosted rollout security review not required per current scope.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): enable feature for 5 internal customers and 3 pilot customers for 2 weeks; monitor errors/latency and overdraft debt accumulation.
Phase 1: enable for all new customers and opt-in existing customers via Console toggle; provide migration compatibility mode for 30 days.
Phase 2: automatic migration for remaining customers with 7-day rollback window and automated email notice; finance reconciliation for first billing cycle post-migration.
Phase 3: retrospective and adjustments to decay rates / caps based on observed utilization and invoice disputes.

Rollback criteria: >2% of requests returning unexpected 5xx attributable to overdraft logic, >0.5% invoice dispute rate linked to overdraft in canary => rollback to previous global soft-overage model.
Communications: prepare help center article, customer-facing changelog, and a partner note for reseller teams prior to Phase 1.
testing_plan: Unit tests for ledger arithmetic, decay functions (half-life/linear), and race conditions under concurrency.
Integration tests covering API responses, Console display, billing export columns and reconciliation script for sample datasets.
Load tests simulating multi-tenant bursts to validate latency impact and deadlock-free overdraft contention.
Chaos testing: inject delayed ledger writes and verify idempotency and correctness of audit logs.
Customer acceptance tests run with pilot customers and documented sign-off template.
metrics_kpis: % of burst events served without generating a support ticket (goal >= 85% by end of Q2)
Average overdraft utilization per-customer (target < 30% for stable plans)
Number of invoice disputes attributed to overdraft accounting per 1k customers (target < 2)
P50/P95 latency delta introduced by overdraft check (target < 5ms added)
Time to reconcile overdraft ledger to invoice (target < 24 hours after billing run)
decision_log: 2026-02-24 Marcus Lee: choose time-decay model (half-life default 24h) over fixed window credits to better smooth multi-day spikes.
2026-02-27 Engineering review (Luca Chen): recommended conservative default overdraft caps (20-50% of baseline) to limit financier exposure.
2026-03-03 Finance (Olivia Martinez): require explicit CSV export fields for per-bucket overdraft and a reconciliation endpoint for automated ingestion.
2026-03-08 PM review (Priya Shah): add simulation mode and Console override after pilot feedback to expedite MVP adoption.
notes: Trade-offs: overdraft reduces immediate friction but increases short-term finance exposure; mitigation via caps, decay and conservative defaults.
Edge cases: customers with multiple active orgs under one billing entity should have configurable aggregation window (default=per-org).
Open question: whether to bill overdraft usage immediately or incorporate into next invoice cycle with flagged line items (finance prefers next-invoice).
Monitoring: add SLOs for ledger update failure rate (<0.01%) and reconciliation mismatch rate (<0.1%).
